question: After the current-head test blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw core accept signed hosted marketplace feed refresh with local Ed25519 trust anchors, threshold enforcement, fail-closed signed profiles, and persisted snapshot trust state?
rationale: The implementation changes how hosted marketplace feed content becomes trusted and how trust evidence is persisted; that security and rollout policy cannot be settled by code review alone.

options.title: Approve the trust stack in order
options.body: Fix the current test blocker, land or approve the verifier and signed-config predecessors first, then re-review this refresh slice against the combined trust boundary.

options.title: Request trust-model changes
options.body: Ask for changes to fail-closed behavior, documentation, or persisted trust-state shape before signed refresh enters core.

options.title: Pause signed-feed trust
options.body: Keep the stack paused if maintainers do not want signed hosted marketplace feed trust in OpenClaw core right now.

recommendation.title: Approve the trust stack in order
recommendation.body: Fix the current test blocker, land or approve the verifier and signed-config predecessors first, then re-review this refresh slice against the combined trust boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a persisted-state and security-boundary acceptance decision, and steipete is the strongest current routing candidate from state/config history and maintainer context.
